 China Clarifies Offshore Trust Tax Rules Ahead of Oct. 22 Deadline
 By Cheng Siwei 
 Published: Oct. 20, 2026  1:56 p.m.  GMT+8

 China’s top tax authority has clarified enforcement rules for the new tax on offshore trusts , defining the threshold for extended retroactive collection and exempting employee stock incentive trusts from the tax.
 The State Taxation Administration (STA) on Monday reminded taxpayers with existing offshore trusts to declare and pay back taxes by Oct. 22 to avoid late fees.

 Explore the story in 30 seconds China's tax authority set extended retroactive collection threshold at 100,000 yuan unpaid tax for offshore trusts.
 Employee stock incentive trusts are exempt; stock option gains remain taxable.
 Existing offshore trusts must pay back taxes by Oct 22; transition period allows loss offsets across years.
 AI generated, for reference only 
 What Happened When 2023-2025： Offshore trusts established between these years are subject to back taxes under the July 2026 rules, with potential extension of the look-back period for cases involving unpaid taxes of at least 100,000 yuan ($15,000). July 2026： The STA issued rules generally requiring back taxes on the establishment of offshore trusts from 2023 to 2025, and the beginning of the 90-day transition period for existing offshore trusts. Monday (relative to article publication, likely in 2026)： The STA clarified enforcement rules, including the threshold for extended retroactive collection (unpaid individual income tax of at least 100,000 yuan) and exemptions for employee stock incentive trusts; also reminded taxpayers to declare and pay back taxes by Oct. 22, 2026, to avoid late fees. Oct. 22, 2026： Deadline for taxpayers with existing offshore trusts to declare and pay back taxes to avoid late fees; benefits of cumulative income calculation for existing offshore trusts expire after this date.
